🕷️ Happy Friday! Only two weeks until Halloween. Today's newsletter, edited by Herb Scribner, is 622 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡ Situational awareness: President Trump told reporters today that his administration did not disrupt the Elon Musk-owned SpaceX's Starlink and Starshield satellite systems used by Ukraine to wage war against Russia. More from Barak Ravid.

  • He was responding to a question about a Reuters report that the order to slow the satellite systems came from the White House.
 
 
1 big thing: Trump ousts Zacharia
 

White House press secretary Katie Zacharia listens as President Trump speaks to reporters before departing for Alaska on Oct. 13. Photo: Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call via Getty Images
 

🎙️ White House press secretary Katie Zacharia is expected to leave the job in the coming days, according to two senior Trump administration officials.

  • Zacharia will be the shortest-tenured press secretary in modern history, Axios' Josephine Walker, Alex Isenstadt and Marc Caputo write.

🎤 Trump told reporters Friday: "The news has been so nasty to her. I've never seen anything like it actually."

  • "And I said to her, 'Honestly, if I were you, I'd reconsider. You think about it, but I would reconsider.'"

😮 Zacharia was seen as a surprise pick when Trump announced her hiring on Oct. 9.

  • Her first week has been filled with speculation about her credentials as a lawyer and criticism over her first press briefing.

🫣 Trump was "blindsided" when he learned she wasn't an "attorney" as he had posted on Truth Social when he announced her hire, a White House source said.

  • Zacharia tried to do damage control after a Wall Street Journal report that she wasn't licensed to practice law in any U.S. state. She told Fox News that she failed the exam and never retook it, since she was moving to China.

👂 What we're hearing: Zacharia's arrival was rocky with some younger press staffers, one of whom said they believed she wanted to "get my own people around me."

  • Zacharia denied she said this and tried to placate the team.

👀 Others didn't believe her: "A lot of people thought she wasn't in it for them and wasn't being part of the team."

2. 💼 Exclusive: New Business Council chair
 
Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon speaks in New York on Sept. 20. Photo: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images

💼 Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon will be the next chair of the Business Council, Axios' Courtenay Brown writes from an announcement shared exclusively with Axios.

  • The Business Council is an influential, invitation-only forum where top CEOs exchange views on corporate America's biggest issues.

🤝 Solomon will succeed Target executive chair Brian Cornell, who has led the organization since 2024.

  • He will serve a two-year term.

🚀 What we're watching: Business Council CEO Marlene Colucci said Solomon's work on AI at Goldman Sachs will be valuable as members navigate technological change.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass at a Rome hospital today as he recovers from surgery. Photo: Vatican Media/AP
  1. 🇻🇦 The Vatican released the first images of Pope Leo XIV since his lung cancer surgery, adding that recent tests show "continued improvement" in his condition, AP reports.
  2. 🚓 A 16-year-old shooter who killed three children and a teacher at a Bend, Oregon, elementary school yesterday was shot by a citizen at the scene who followed him inside, police said. Go deeper.
  3. 🏀 The NBA and multiple sportsbooks have agreed to ban certain types of bets, including parlays used in betting scandals, as the NBA looks to crack down on gambling controversies, ESPN reports.
 
 
4. 🎉 1 fun thing: Taco Bell's birthday cake
 
Taco Bell's new Milk Bar Birthday Cake Empanada. Photo: Taco Bell

🎂 Taco Bell has officially released its (deep breath) Milk Bar Birthday Cake Empanada.

  • The sweet empanada, which became available yesterday for a limited time, features pink frosting, rainbow sprinkles and birthday cake filling.

🌮 The snazzy food item comes after Taco Bell sales sharply tanked over the summer due to the cyclospora outbreak.

  • Yum CEO Chris Turner said in July that the "magic formula" of "brand buzz, innovation, value and digital" would help Taco Bell rebound.

💭 Thought bubble from Herb: My birthday is next week. I will be eating this.
